title: What kind of triangle has sides four, four and six?
description: A base of six centimetres is drawn and the same compass opening of four centimetres is used from both ends, and the triangle is then named by its equal sides. Keeko doubts the name and says all three sides are equal because two of them are four.
teaching_notes: One idea: two equal sides mean one compass opening is used at both ends of the base, and a triangle with exactly two equal sides is isosceles. Watch for children who say all three sides are equal because two of them match.

source: Construct a triangle with sidelengths 4 cm, 4 cm and 6 cm and say what kind of triangle it is.
video_script.why: The child has built a triangle with three equal sides and one with three different sides, and now builds one with exactly two equal sides.
video_script.substitution: The base is the longest side, six centimetres, and both arcs have the same opening of four centimetres.
video_script.anchor: A triangle with sides of four, four and six centimetres, and its kind
video_script.wrong_move: A child sees two sides of four centimetres and says all three sides are equal, though the base measures six centimetres.
video_script.payoff_line: The triangle with sides four, four and six centimetres is isosceles.

final_answer.spoken: an isosceles triangle with sides four, four and six centimetres

never_show: the word isosceles before the answer beat
maths_rules: arc from A with radius 4 cm: every place on it is 4 cm from A
arc from B with radius 4 cm: every place on it is 4 cm from B
C is on both arcs, so AC = 4 cm and BC = 4 cm
AC = BC = 4 cm and AB = 6 cm, so exactly two sides are equal and the triangle is isosceles
video_script.design: One idea: the same compass opening used at both ends of the base gives two equal sides. One base, two arcs of the same opening, and the name; Keeko's doubt closes the video.
